conventions.convention: The curve setting is an arbitrary field k and a smooth proper geometrically integral curve C. Divisors are finite signed sums of closed points, degree is weighted by [κ(p):k], and positive coefficients permit poles in O_C(D).
Under the stated Axiom of Choice, l(D)=dim_k L(D)=h^0(D), and h^i(D)=dim_k H^i(C,O_C(D)). These dimensions are finite; AC also supplies inherited DC premises.
g(C)=h^1(C,O_C)=1−χ(C,O_C); i(D)=h^1(C,O_C(D)). Nonspecial means i(D)=0, equivalently equality in the Riemann inequality.
On P¹, t=x₁/x₀, infinity is [0:1]=V(x₀), and the origin is [1:0]=V(x₁). Thus O(1)≅O([infinity]).
The vanishing threshold is divisor-order positivity D≥D₀+n₀A in a fixed effective ample direction O_C(A)≅φ*O(1), with φ finite. It is not a threshold depending only on deg D.
For nonempty |D|, its dimension means the Krull dimension of Proj(Sym_k(L(D)∨)), not a dimension assigned to its set of k-rational points.
Nevanlinna proximity uses the normalized chordal distance of diameter one. Counts use closed discs and the centre term n(0,a;f) log r; integrated counts can be negative for r<1.

With Countable Choice, S(r,f) is bounded in absolute value by C(log⁺T(r,f)+log r) outside a measurable set of finite linear measure. Constants, thresholds and exceptional sets belong to each occurrence; finite unions suffice.

Reduced counting counts each preimage once; N₁(r,a;f) counts local-degree surplus at one target, while N₁(r,f) counts all ramification. Deficiency and ramification indices use liminf, and target sums are suprema of finite subsums.
An oriented full lattice basis satisfies Im(ω₂/ω₁)>0. The transition matrix in the lattice definition uses columns: ω′_j=Σ_k a_kj ω_k.
Weierstrass sums and products are unordered finite-subset limits. The normalizations are g₂=60G₄, g₃=140G₆, σ′(0)=1 and full-period η_j=2ζ(ω_j/2), with η₁ω₂−η₂ω₁=2πi.
The primitive-period sigma sign is −1. For ω=mω₁+nω₂, the general sign is (−1)^(m+n+mn), with η_ω=mη₁+nη₂.
The cubic is Y²Z=4X³−g₂XZ²−g₃Z³, its identity is O=[0:1:0], and inversion on the affine chart sends (x,y) to (x,−y).
Reduced ratios satisfy Im τ>0, −1/2<Re τ≤1/2, |τ|≥1, and additionally Re τ≥0 when |τ|=1.

load_bearing.statement: For a full complex lattice with oriented basis, the defining ℘ sum converges absolutely and normally off the lattice, independently of enumeration. ℘ is even and lattice-periodic, with double poles exactly at lattice points and principal part (z−λ)^−2. Its derivative is −2Σ_{ω∈Λ}(z−ω)^−3, normally convergent off Λ, odd and lattice-periodic.

Assume AC. For a divisor D and closed point p on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k, the inclusion O_C(D)→O_C(D+p) fits into a short exact sequence with skyscraper cokernel isomorphic to i_{p,*}κ(p). Its H⁰ has k-dimension [κ(p):k] and its higher cohomology vanishes. For effective E, the analogous coherent cokernel Q_E has dim_k H⁰(C,Q_E)=deg_k E and H^q(C,Q_E)=0 for q≥1.

Assume Countable Choice. For nonconstant meromorphic f on C, m₀(r,f′/f)=S(r,f), and the normalized chordal proximity to infinity obeys the same bound. For finite-order f the bound is O_f(log r) at every sufficiently large radius; for rational f it is O_f(1) at every sufficiently large radius.

Assume Countable Choice. For nonconstant meromorphic f on C and distinct sphere values a₁,…,a_q, q≥3, outside a set of finite linear measure: Σ_j m(r,a_j;f)+N₁(r,f)≤2T(r,f)+S(r,f), equivalently (q−2)T≤Σ_j N(r,a_j;f)−N₁(r,f)+S(r,f), and consequently (q−2)T≤Σ_j N̄(r,a_j;f)+S(r,f). The errors are O_f(log r) at all sufficiently large radii for finite-order f and O_f(1) there for rational f.

For a full complex lattice, the torus map ℘ has degree two. ℘(z)=℘(w) iff w≡z or w≡−z modulo Λ. Its critical classes are exactly [0], [ω₁/2], [ω₂/2], [(ω₁+ω₂)/2], with distinct branch values infinity,e₁,e₂,e₃. The zeros of ℘′ are exactly the translates of the three nonzero half-periods, each simple.

Assume AC. For every divisor D on a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k, l(D)−i(D)=h⁰(C,O_C(D))−h¹(C,O_C(D))=deg_k(D)+1−g. Moreover i(D)≥0, so l(D)≥deg_k(D)+1−g, with equality iff i(D)=0; i(0)=g. No duality identification or degree threshold is asserted.

Assume AC. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k, φ:C→P¹_k finite, and A effective with O_C(A)≅φ*O(1). For every divisor D₀ there is an integer n₀ such that H¹(C,O_C(D₀+nA+E))=0 for every n≥n₀ and every effective E; equivalently h¹(D)=0 for every D≥D₀+n₀A.

For a full complex lattice, the associated projective Weierstrass cubic is nonsingular with unique point at infinity O=[0:1:0]. The map [z]↦[℘(z):℘′(z):1] away from [0] extends holomorphically by [0]↦O and is a bijective biholomorphism.

concerns.concern: Fact F5 and proof 6.3 require Lund–Ye Theorem A2, printed p. 552, for a one-sided exterior domain with a finite-linear-measure exceptional set. I could not verify its full statement: the linked SciEngine PDF was inaccessible, and the [publisher page](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11425-010-0037-3) supplied only a subscription preview. The current research/frontier-37-owner-30-alpha-i-5a.md records this same prerequisite as open and escalated. The plane lemma does not supply the exterior assertion. Exact source evidence or a proved replacement remains necessary; this does not assert that the external theorem is false.

Fact F6 says: 'f has order ρ<∞ exactly when T(r,f)≤r^{ρ+1} for all large r'. The converse is false for a specified ρ. For f(z)=exp(z²), T(r,f)=r²/π+O(1), so the displayed bound holds with ρ=1 although the order is 2. The cited order definition uses a limsup. The proof needs only the forward eventual-growth bound.

The 'Zeros and poles' remark says that zeros and poles of a Λ-elliptic function are isolated on the torus and have finitely many classes. The definition explicitly includes constants, hence f≡0. Its zero set is the entire torus and is not isolated. The zero/divisor discussion needs a nonzero-function qualification.

The displayed boundary definition is '{b+s+ti:s∈{0,1} or t∈{0,1}}', without 0≤s,t≤1. Literally this is four complete lines, not the boundary of P_b. The proof uses four bounded segments and local finiteness of their translates. The missing parameter restriction affects the defined set.

Two short derivations need completion. In 2.2, trace zero gives u=−a/b, not immediately u=0; the reduced-domain inequalities must first force |b|=1 and a=0. In 7.1, the case |τ*|>1 is declared already reduced despite allowing Re τ*=−1/2 from 5.1; τ*=−1/2+2i illustrates the omitted translation to the right boundary. Both conclusions are recoverable by elementary finite calculations.

Proof 2.1 infers uniform convergence on 'the closed annulus 0<|z|≤R' from normal convergence off Λ. This punctured set is not compact. Uniform convergence through zero follows instead from the corrected-summand tail estimate already proved by the ℘ supplier, or its explicit principal-part argument; that justification should replace the inference.

Proof 5.1 says that for fixed arbitrary w the expression W(z,w) is meromorphic in z 'by the same argument' as 4.1. When w∈Λ, the separate constants ℘(w) and ℘′(w) are poles, so that argument cannot literally define W. The combined right-hand expression must first be continued in w, as opposed to substituting into its separate terms. The stated meromorphic-continuation interpretation makes the intended result recoverable.

Proof 1.2 gives [[1,1],[0,1]] for (1+i,i) relative to (1,i). This is a row-coefficient convention, whereas def-complex-lattice-and-complex-torus explicitly fixes columns ω′_j=Σ_k a_kjω_k, under which the matrix is [[1,0],[1,1]]. State the row convention here or align the displayed matrix with the definition.

The opening summary lists Im τ>0, −1/2<Re τ≤1/2 and |τ|≥1 and says the reduced ratio is unique. The item correctly adds Re τ≥0 on |τ|=1, but the page summary omits it. Without that boundary rule, τ=3/10+i√91/10 and −1/τ are distinct allowed ratios for the same lattice. Include the item's boundary qualification.

seams_checked.note: The consuming text states the local-equation sheaf construction, rational-section dictionary, principal kernel, principal degree-zero result and Picard degree descent with their actual domains. Positive divisors permit poles, and AC supplies the declared DC routes. No stronger pullback or arbitrary-scheme Cartier/Weil comparison is consumed.

The consuming claims preserve smooth/proper/geometrically integral curve hypotheses over arbitrary k, weighted residue degrees, the DVR order convention, L(D)=H⁰(O_C(D)), finite locally free pole-map degree and fibre statements, and degree-one birational isomorphism. The conic and cubic examples establish the required curve geometry before using genus suppliers.

The downstream facts state l−i=deg+1−g, l=h⁰, i=h¹, the genus normalization, torsion-free coherent sheaf local freeness, degree-zero section triviality, and the point-addition sequence faithfully under the consumers' stated AC and curve hypotheses. Sharp degree thresholds are obtained using additional duality suppliers, not attributed to this group's fixed-direction vanishing theorem.
